# PCM quality: 0.6.0

pysacd 0.6.0's PCM output against 0.5.5's, measured with dsd-measure 0.1.3 (release v0.1.3, commit 8010bba) on the same machine with the same inputs, from the [pinned suite](../../suites/pysacd.toml). A change larger than the bound is flagged.

Default settings for both versions: for 0.6.0 the precise filter with the standard cutoff (40 kHz) at both rates.
Default cutoff 40 kHz at every rate: at 176.4 kHz wide (80 kHz) measures within 0.3 dB of it on SINAD,
THD and the 20 Hz to 20 kHz noise floor, and above 40 kHz passes mostly DSD's ultrasonic noise;
choose it with `--pcm-cutoff wide`.

**Conclusion.** 0.6.0 measures the same as or better than 0.5.5: the changes beyond repeatability are improvements or a null less deep than the candidate's re-run gives.

## Filters

Each filter and cutoff pysacd 0.6.0 offers, stereo FLAC, the same dsd-measure version (0.1.3), inputs and
wrapper as above ([suites/pysacd-filters.toml](../../suites/pysacd-filters.toml)), with 0.5.5 from
the table above for reference. SINAD and THD are with a 1 kHz tone at 0 dB SACD; the noise floor
is 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

| Rate | Filter, cutoff | SINAD (dB) | THD (dB) | Noise floor (dBFS) | Alias rejection (dB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 88.2 kHz | precise, standard (40 kHz), the default | 141.8 | -160.4 | -148.9 | -156.7 |
| 88.2 kHz | pysacd (0.5.x response, -3 dB at 43.3 kHz) | 127.9 | -147.6 | -130.7 | -132.4 |
| 88.2 kHz | 0.5.5 | 127.8 | -146.4 | -130.7 | -132.4 |
| 176.4 kHz | precise, standard (40 kHz), the default | 143.6 | -161.9 | -151.5 | -162.1 |
| 176.4 kHz | precise, wide (80 kHz) | 143.6 | -162.1 | -151.4 | -163.5 |
| 176.4 kHz | pysacd (0.5.x response, -3 dB at 71.7 kHz) | 128.2 | -148.3 | -130.8 | -139.2 |
| 176.4 kHz | 0.5.5 | 128.1 | -147.6 | -130.8 | -139.3 |

Precise measures 13.9 to 15.4 dB better SINAD than the pysacd filter at both rates. At 176.4 kHz
the standard and wide cutoffs measure within 0.3 dB of each other on SINAD, THD and the noise floor
(SINAD and THD at the measurement's floor or the 24-bit word length), and the wide cutoff's worst
alias image is 1.4 dB lower. The pysacd filter in 0.6.0 (computed in double precision) measures
within 0.2 dB of 0.5.5 on SINAD and the noise floor, and 0.7 dB (176.4 kHz) to 1.2 dB (88.2 kHz)
lower THD, within the 1.7 dB THD bound. The −3 dB points are measured with tones
through the engine ([converting](../converting.md#pcm-filters-and-cutoffs)).

## Out-of-band level and file size

What each filter and cutoff leaves above the audio band, and what it costs in file size, on real
music: one stereo track of a commercial SACD (jazz, 4 min 45 s, plain DSD64), converted with each
setting, band power summed over both channels in dBFS (a full-scale sine is 0 dBFS), and the
FLAC file's size (`--flac-level` 5). The same track and settings for 0.5.5 and 0.6.0, one run each
(the precise filter is deterministic). This section was measured on the 0.6.0 candidate build, dsd2pcm 0.2.0's release candidate (commit e6ba8ba); it was not re-run on the 0.2.0 tag.

| Rate | Output | 20–40 kHz (dBFS) | 40–50 kHz (dBFS) | 50–60 kHz (dBFS) | 60–70 kHz (dBFS) | 70–80 kHz (dBFS) | 80–88.2 kHz (dBFS) | FLAC (MB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 176.4 kHz | 0.5.5 | −68.6 | −61.5 | −52.9 | −46.5 | −48.7 | −74.2 | 207.1 |
| 176.4 kHz | precise, standard (default) | −68.6 | −71.6 | −155.5 | −155.5 | −155.5 | −156.4 | 137.9 |
| 176.4 kHz | precise, wide | −68.6 | −61.5 | −52.9 | −46.1 | −41.6 | −45.5 | 212.9 |
| 176.4 kHz | precise, low | −72.1 | −155.5 | −155.5 | −155.5 | −155.5 | −156.4 | 100.7 |
| 176.4 kHz | pysacd | −68.6 | −61.5 | −52.9 | −46.5 | −48.7 | −74.2 | 207.1 |

| Rate | Output | 20–40 kHz (dBFS) | 40–44.1 kHz (dBFS) | FLAC (MB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 88.2 kHz | 0.5.5 | −68.6 | −70.2 | 94.47 |
| 88.2 kHz | precise, standard (default) | −68.6 | −71.6 | 94.34 |
| 88.2 kHz | precise, low | −72.1 | −156.4 | 86.73 |
| 88.2 kHz | pysacd | −68.6 | −70.2 | 94.47 |

The 20 Hz to 20 kHz band measures −24.0 dBFS for every row. Above the precise filter's stopband the
level is that of 24-bit rounding (about −155 dBFS per band). At 176.4 kHz, 0.6.0's default removes
what 0.5.5 passed above about 40 kHz: on this track −52.9 to −46.5 dBFS per 10 kHz band between
50 and 80 kHz, about 100 dB above the 24-bit floor, mostly the DSD modulator's shaped noise, whose
level rises with frequency. Its FLAC
file is 33 % smaller than 0.5.5's and 35 % smaller than the wide cutoff's. Choose
`--pcm-cutoff wide` to keep the band to 80 kHz, or `--pcm-filter pysacd` for 0.5.x's response.
At 88.2 kHz the default keeps the same band as 0.5.5 (the response is 3 dB down at 42.6 kHz
against 43.3 kHz) and the files are the same size.

## Notes

- Inputs: identical for both versions (SHA-256 of every file fed to pysacd); null-test source SHA-256 `5defb0279817a927`.
- Output format, read by dsd-measure from each file: stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz DSD64 in, 24-bit integer out at 88.2 kHz; stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz DSD64 in, 24-bit integer out at 176.4 kHz; 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz DSD64 in, 24-bit integer out at 88.2 kHz; 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz DSD64 in, 24-bit integer out at 176.4 kHz, the same for 0.5.5 and 0.6.0 on every output.
- Word length: SINAD of stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz (candidate); stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz (candidate); 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz (candidate); 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz (candidate) lies within 6 dB of the SINAD that the output's integer word length allows (dsd-measure's "Not judged: output format"); it describes the file format as much as the converter, and both versions write the same format. Marked [word length].
- Reference floor: figures within 6 dB of dsd-measure's reference floor, limited by the measurement (dsd-measure's names; those in the table are marked [floor]): stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz previous: imd_ccif, jtest, peak_sinad; stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz candidate: imd_ccif, imd_smpte, jtest, multitone, peak_sinad, sinad, thd, thdn; stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz previous: imd_ccif, jtest, peak_sinad; stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz candidate: dr, imd_ccif, imd_smpte, jtest, multitone, peak_sinad, sinad, thd, thdn, thdn_a; 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz previous: imd_ccif, jtest, peak_sinad; 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz candidate: imd_ccif, imd_smpte, jtest, multitone, peak_sinad, sinad, thd, thdn; 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz previous: imd_ccif, jtest, peak_sinad; 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz candidate: dr, imd_ccif, imd_smpte, jtest, multitone, peak_sinad, sinad, thd, thdn, thdn_a.
- Repeatability: largest spread over three runs of the candidate with the signal shifted by idle frames, per figure: sinad 0.00 dB, thd 0.00 dB, noise 0.00 dB, alias 0.00 dB. For a dithered filter (pysacd) the runs are other dither draws; for an undithered one (precise) they are deterministic re-runs, so the spread is the measurement's, not the converter's.
- Null depth: stereo FLAC 88.2 kHz 82.9 dB (the candidate against its own re-run: 364.5 dB); stereo FLAC 176.4 kHz 82.9 dB (the candidate against its own re-run: 364.5 dB); 5.1 WAV 88.2 kHz 82.9 dB (the candidate against its own re-run: 364.5 dB); 5.1 WAV 176.4 kHz 82.9 dB (the candidate against its own re-run: 364.5 dB). The re-run reference is the measurement's floor for an undithered filter (the same samples, shifted) and two dither draws for a dithered one; the null against the previous release is judged against it.
- Null depth at 176.4 kHz: with the standard cutoff as the default, the null against 0.5.5 aligns as at 88.2 kHz (82.9 dB at both rates; the difference is the change of filter and timing).
- Timing: 0.6.0's default output is centred on the DSD timeline; 0.5.x output was late by 0.266 samples (3.01 µs) at 88.2 kHz and early by 0.469 samples (2.66 µs) at 176.4 kHz, a constant group-delay offset of its filter (measured on the candidate build, not re-run on the tag). So a track converted by 0.5.x and one by 0.6.0 don't align sample-exactly. Measured from the phase of a 1 kHz and a 7 kHz sine that start at phase 0 on the first DSD bit (first-order modulator, no delay in its signal path): precise is at 0.000 samples (within 0.001) at both rates; 0.5.5 and `--pcm-filter pysacd` at +0.266 and −0.469. The `pysacd` filter keeps the old timing. Gain is the same to 0.001 dB.
- Candidate build, for the out-of-band section and the timing note only: dsd2pcm built from the 0.2.0 candidate's C library source archive (commit e6ba8ba, SHA-256 `019aa8c2…`), the pin in dsd2pcm.lock; Linux x86-64, Ryzen 9 3950X, one worker thread, shared machine; timings are not measured here.
- Build: dsd2pcm 0.2.0 (tag v0.2.0, commit b743111), built from the release's C library source archive (SHA-256 `a842ca6e…`), the pin in dsd2pcm.lock; Linux x86-64, one worker thread, shared machine; timings are not measured here.
- Alias rejection and dsd-measure's version: the worst alias image of 0.6.0 measures 2.6 to 3.0 dB less rejection with dsd-measure 0.1.3 than the draft of this page measured with 0.1.2 (0.5.5 moved by 0.0 to 0.2 dB), although pysacd's output is byte-identical between the two builds (the 122 PCM goldens are unchanged). dsd-measure 0.1.3's reference modulator draws a different stimulus bitstream, and an alias figure below about −150 dB, under the modulator's own noise, varies by about ±2 dB from one stimulus draw to the next; a filter limited by its own leakage, as 0.5.5's is, varies by about 0.25 dB at most. The repeatability bound above holds the stimulus fixed, so it doesn't show this. Compare alias figures below about −150 dB only within one dsd-measure version.
- Builds: 0.5.5 is `pysacd-0.5.5-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl` (SHA-256 `4d23cd456b11f41582ec54e9a9a7972c38495a3a9677c092d212231a91a63658`); 0.6.0 is the release-0.6.0-dsd2pcm02 branch at commit `f6daf8043d90aeafab5c154d16f995b03d8a324c`, source SHA-256 `d74c940813358d95`.
